summary: Seema Alavi is a historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She taught at the University of Delhi (~1994–2008), served as professor at Jamia Millia Islamia (~2008–2014), and joined Ashoka University as professor around 2020.

Seema K. Chauhan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was a PhD student at the University of Chicago (attested 2017). She served as the Asoke Kumar Sarkar Early Career Fellow in Classical Indology at Balliol College, Oxford.

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) was a scholar in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) under Umpei Shinma and Kanō Tomonobu. He later served as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905) there.

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1925–1928, doctorate 1962) under Kosaku Hamada, later serving as an assistant professor at its Institute for Research in Humanities and university professor (1949–1968).

Seiichi Yagi is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held academic posts at Kanto Gakuin University (~1961–1968), Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1989), and Toin University of Yokohama (~1989–1997).

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) studied law and Buddhist philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917, doctorate 1933) under Eiichi Makino, Daito Shimaji, and others. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986), where he later held a post (attested 1990), and served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2005–2008) and became a professor there around 2013.
Seiji Nemoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2004–2015).
Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1968–1976) and Asia University (~1976–1984).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1981). He later returned to Komazawa University, serving as a professor around 2003.

Seikaku Hirata (1924–2008) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He held an academic post at Hanazono University (~1979–1990).

Sein Tin (1899–1942) was a Burmese scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rangoon (~1917–1921) under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927) and at Christ Church, Oxford (~1927–1930).
Seiran Ouchi (1845–1918) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as a lecturer (jiko) at Nishi Hongan-ji and later was president of Toyo University (1914–1918).

Seiren Matsunami (1912–1989) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (-1930) under Walther Schubring and Naoshiro Tsuji. He was a professor at Kyushu University (attested 1965) and Rissho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima (1957–2019) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology scholar. He studied at Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking universities under Minoru Hara, K. R. Norman, Oskar von Hinüber, and Xianlin Ji, later serving as professor at Soka University (~1996–2019).

Seishin Kato (1872–1956) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), president of Taisho University (1940), and president of Toyo University (1952, 1955).
Seitatsu Matsunami is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida (1922–2006) was a Zen Buddhist scholar and Sinologist who studied at Hanazono and Otani universities. He held multiple posts at Hanazono University (1949–1995), directed its IRIZ (~1988–1996), and was a professor at Kyoto University (1976–1986).

Semen Ivanovich Tyulyaev (1898–1993) was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Moscow State University (~1921–1927). He was a researcher at the State Museum of Oriental Art (1927–1958) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1958–1961), also teaching at MSU (1948–1956).
